newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees no reason to alter economic policy.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees no reason to alter economic policy.

text.p: Brazil's Economic Policy secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros said October's bigger than expected $1.308 billion trade deficit was not a reason for changing macroeconomic policy.
"What we think is there is no reason to change anything in the structure of macroeconomic policy," Mendonca de Barros told reporters.
"This result must be seen in the context of the Plano Real (economic stabilisation plan)."
He blamed the deficit on seasonal demand and the natural process of opening the economy and said he believed economic policy was on track.
"By the end of 1996 what we will have is consolidation (of the plan) without the process having ended. The structure of economic policy carries on," he said.

Mendonca de Barros acknowleged, without making any predictions for the trade balance in November or by year-end, that the final months of the year were "seasonally the most aggressive moments for the trade balance."
October's $1.308 billion trade deficit was the biggest in Brazilian history.
The figure raised questions about the government's commitment to relaxing monetary policy and to the current trade tariff structure.
Forecasts for the October trade deficit had ranged from $900 million to $1.0 billion.
